1.pericope_label: I will love thee, O LORD, my strength

debates.q: What is the occasion of the psalm?

sides.view: A song of the Messiah composed when David’s wars were over, in five parts
David’s whole life of danger, from the flight before Saul to the wars of his old age
Christ’s, on the names: David is strong of hand and Saul is demanding
The inscription was originally short; the rest is narrative framing

debates.q: What are the sorrows that compassed him?

sides.view: Cords, though Samuel’s waves of death is probably the true reading
Cables — the stratagems in which he was nearly taken
Deadly troubles breaking in like a flood
The snares laid for David, and beyond him the griefs of Christ

outliers.view: Renders the horn of salvation as a peak of safety, on the ground that mountain peaks are called horns in many languages
Infers from the psalm’s delivery to the precentor that a good man’s private compositions may serve the public

7.pericope_label: Then the earth shook and trembled; the foundations also of the hills moved

debates.q: Is the theophany a described storm or a figure?

sides.view: A storm tracked stage by stage, from the first rumbling to the wind’s effects on the ground
A real tempest and earthquake, with observed parallels from natural history
Figurative throughout, denoting the greatness of God’s anger
A thunderstorm borrowed from the imagery of Sinai

debates.q: What is the cherub he rides on?

sides.view: Cloud shaped into giant pinions; and the word may be a transposition for chariot
The conjecture is noted but resisted; the word points to a griffin-like seizing creature
The angels, whom God employs in raising storms

outliers.view: Illustrates the laying bare of the channels from a Jamaican earthquake in which rivers poured from the chasms and new lakes covered a thousand acres
Carries the storm on a chain of five poetic quotations, ancient and modern, in the space of nine verses

16.pericope_label: He sent from above, he took me, he drew me out of many waters

sides.view: The giant’s son who nearly killed David when he was exhausted, and from whom Abishai rescued him
The Philistine champion or Saul, and beyond them Satan and death

debates.q: What is the large place he is brought into?

sides.view: A historical allusion to the settlement of Israel in Canaan
A country cleared of enemies who had cooped him in holes and corners
Freedom and comfort after straits, ascribed wholly to God’s good pleasure
Heaven, spacious enough for Christ and all his people

outliers.view: Reads the rescue as effected by the very storm sent against the enemies, with the gates of death lying under the parted floods
Fixes the verse on one recorded incident, after which David’s men forbade him the battlefield

20.pericope_label: The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness

debates.q: How can David claim to be rewarded for his righteousness?

sides.view: Providence has a rule of justice distinct from the spiritual kingdom, where grace reigns alone
It cannot be his own righteousness at all, which is filthy rags and merits nothing
The deliverances acquitted him at the bar of men, not of God
It means his conduct towards Saul, whose blood he refused to shed

debates.q: What is the iniquity he kept himself from?

sides.view: The easily-besetting sin of his constitution — and what it was is useless to conjecture
The sin he was most inclined or tempted to
A question that does not arise, since the uprightness is fully true only of Christ

outliers.view: Draws a line between providential reward and spiritual grace, allowing an honest man to know he is honest without self-righteousness
Refuses to guess at David’s besetting sin, calling the question a subject of useless conjecture

25.pericope_label: With the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful

debates.q: How can God shew himself froward?

sides.view: The verb means to twist and wrestle: God will follow the crooked man through all his windings
Two twisting roots stand behind one English word; God turns away from those who turn away
He will cross him and walk contrary to him

debates.q: What is the lamp that God lights?

sides.view: Life itself, and by extension the continuance of David’s house
The family preserved from extinction, and perhaps the Messiah
Prosperity, spiritual light, or the estate of Christ’s kingdom

outliers.view: Recovers the original sense of the English word wicked as crooked, by way of a mediaeval Psalter rendering
Notes that David’s military skill was neither bred nor natural to him, his genius running to music and poetry instead

30.pericope_label: As for God, his way is perfect: the word of the LORD is tried

sides.view: Yes — the verse shows it, and all military skill is God’s gift
No — war is as contrary to the spirit of Christianity as murder

debates.q: Of what metal is the bow?

sides.view: Brass; steel is out of the question, being probably unknown in David’s day
Copper, and the arms bend it — a test of strength like the bow of Ulysses

outliers.view: Turns a verse on being taught to war into a denunciation of Christian nations that shed one another’s blood
Defends calling God meek against the fear of anthropomorphism, asking why meek should be feared where jealous is not

37.pericope_label: I have pursued mine enemies, and overtaken them

sides.view: Two sets — Philistines to their gods, and professing Israelites to the Lord
One set, whose prayer failed because it was for their own cause and too late
Men looking round for help, and crying to idols as the mariners did

debates.q: What is meant by beating them small as dust?

sides.view: A result, not a material — they became as dust, since dust is not pulverized
Sweeping them away; the two texts differ, and the Greek gives grind or pound
Utter and irrecoverable ruin, like the shattered image of the four monarchies
A literal description of how the people of Rabbah were treated

outliers.view: Reads the unanswered cry to the Lord as coming from David’s own countrymen who professed the true worship while opposing him

43.pericope_label: Thou hast delivered me from the strivings of the people

debates.q: Are the strivings domestic or foreign?

sides.view: The parallelism favours the nations, but the other text’s my people points to civil trouble
Domestic — the revolt of Absalom and the war for Ishbosheth
The tribes who withheld allegiance until Hebron, and beyond them Christ’s opponents

debates.q: How do the two copies of the hymn stand to each other?

sides.view: Independent copies of a lost original, this one altered for choir use
The differences are noted verse by verse without a theory of origin

outliers.view: Turns the verse on praise among the heathen into a dating argument, doubting an individual would have spoken so
Quotes an early writer that the psalm is still sung wherever Christians dwell, so that David praises God among the Gentiles to this day
